tips.title: Mastering Panel Line Scribing with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: For deep, consistent panel lines, use RB Productions scribing tools. First, lightly score the panel lines with a pencil, then use the RB Productions scribing tool to cut a continuous, even groove. Hold the tool at a 45° angle, apply even pressure, and maintain a steady speed. For wider lines, use the larger RB tool. Finish with a fine tip marker to darken the lines if desired.

tips.title: Bending Photo-Etch with Eduard Bending Jigs
tips.text: Eduard's photo-etch bending jigs allow precise, repeatable bends. Pre-heat the photo-etch piece with a hairdryer or heat gun, then carefully place it in the jig, bending along the desired line. Hold in place until cooled. For tight radii, use the smallest jig, while larger jigs are better for wider bends.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Maintenance with Iwata's Cleaning Solution
tips.text: Keep your Iwata airbrush performing smoothly with regular needle cleaning. After each use, disassemble the nozzle and needle, soak them in Iwata's Airbrush Cleaner for 15 minutes, then gently scrub with a soft brush. Rinse with water, dry thoroughly, and reassemble. This removes paint residue and prevents clogging.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki Masking Tape
tips.text: Tamiya tape is great for simple, straight masking lines, while Kabuki tape is better for complex curves and delicate applications. For best results, use Tamiya tape for straight lines, and Kabuki for curves. Ensure both tapes are pressed down firmly for a perfect seal. Kabuki tape can be repositioned, making it ideal for tricky areas.

tips.title: Progressive Sanding Sticks for Smooth Surfaces
tips.text: For smooth, seamless surfaces, use a progressive sanding stick set like those from Arma Hobby or ICM. Start with the coarsest grit (e.g., 80) to remove major imperfections, then progressively finer grits to achieve a glass-smooth finish. Sand lightly, in circular motions, and frequently check progress to avoid over-sanding.
